beats.text: The Bayeux Tapestry is a tapestry.
beats.note: The scenes are stitched onto linen, not woven into it. That makes it an embroidery.

beats.context: Roughly its length. Sources give 68.38 metres, made from nine linen panels sewn together.

beats.note: Worked in wool on linen, with dyes made from plant material.
Most scholars favour Canterbury. It was probably commissioned by Odo, Bishop of Bayeux.
A Bayeux Cathedral inventory lists it. That is the earliest known reference.

beats.text: The name stuck. The technique did not.
